messages:
mike: Heads-up — noticed a spike in GPU node launches in us-west1 around 02:32 UTC, looks like ~18 nodes provisioned in 6m, cost alert triggered.
anya: Ugh. which deployment? any HPA events?
jia: HPA metrics showed a custom QPS metric jump for /generate endpoint, but the VPA also had a recommendation loop at the same time. might be HPA + VPA thrashing.
mike: logs: 
```
kubectl get hpa -n inference gen-svc -o yaml
# shows target: custom metric 'qps_per_pod' = 120, current 360, replicas: 3 -> 12
kubectl get vpa -n inference gen-svc-vpa -o yaml
# mode: "Auto", recommendation: cpu: 4, memory: 24Gi
```
jia: if VPA set mode:Auto it's applying evictions/restarts to increase pod resources while HPA scales by metric -> we see more CPU per pod so HPA thinks it still needs more replicas? messy.
sam: CA (cluster autoscaler) got scale-up requests because pods couldn't fit GPU nodes with required resourceProfile=gpu-rtx. CA scaled nodepool gpu-rtx-pool from 6 -> 24.
anya: Was there any taint/affinity change? we recently added nodeSelector: accelerator=rtx and podAffinity for colocated cache.
mike: yes, recent rollout added nodeAffinity hard requirement for accelerator=rtx to ensure inference runs on GPU nodes only.
ops-bot: cost-alert: monthly-projected increase = +$7.5k, triggered by cluster autoscaler activity.
jia: Root cause hypothesis: sudden traffic spike -> HPA (custom qps) scaling out -> VPA in auto increases requests/limits on restart -> pods need larger GPUs or more resources -> CA can't binpack so it spins up GPU nodes -> further HPA triggers due to distribution. Cascade.
anya: Quick mitigation: set VPA mode: "Off" for gen-svc or at least set updatePolicy -> updateMode: "Recreate" -> and disable Auto for now. Also cap HPA maxReplicas to reduce runaway.
sam: We should also smooth the custom metric and add stabilizationWindow in HPA: spec.behavior.scaleUp.stabilizationWindowSeconds = 60 and behavior.scaleDown.stabilizationWindowSeconds = 300.
mike: For immediate rollback I can patch the VPA to mode=Off. Would that avoid restarts?
jia: mode=Off prevents VPA from evicting; yes that should stop VPA-induced resource bumps. Also set pod disruption budgets so CA doesn't evict too many.
anya: Long term: either run VPA only for non-HPA'd pods, or use VPA's resourcePolicy to exclude controlledResources: cpu/memory for this deployment. VPA docs recommend not auto-managing pods under HPA.
sam: Also consider changing HPA metric from absolute qps to per-node or use QueueLength + concurrency to better reflect cluster capacity.
jia: CA tuning: set max-node-provision-time=12m and set scaleDownUtilizationThreshold to 0.55 to avoid immediate scale up/scale down oscillations. Also ensure expander policy is 'least-waste' for GPU pools.
mike: anyone know if the custom metric adapter had a glitch? I saw a spike in metric values reported by kube-metrics-adapter at 02:31:58.
anya: I pulled metrics: grafana panel shows a spike in reported qps_per_pod for gen-svc from 90 -> 420 in a single scrape, but upstream LB metrics show a more modest 3x. adapter could have double-counted retries.
sam: Could be a proxy retry flood from a bad client. We should rate-limit at the ingress for that route.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: rolling-back rollout inference/gen-svc @mike requested
mike: I'm doing quick patch: `kubectl patch vpa gen-svc-vpa -n inference -p '{"spec":{"updatePolicy":{"updateMode":"Off"}}}'`
jia: Also create an HPA override: `kubectl patch hpa gen-svc -n inference -p '{"spec":{"maxReplicas":16}}'`
anya: After patches, cluster-autoscaler events stopped spawning new nodes. provisioning stabilized at 8 nodes. cost alert downgraded.
mike: Follow-ups: 1) add docs: "VPA + HPA guidance" in eng-infra, 2) run a chaos test for metric spikes, 3) add an automated alert that correlates CA scale-up events with VPA recommendation changes.
jia: I'll open a PR with HPA behavior defaults (stabilization windows) and a section to disable VPA for HPA-managed deployments.
sam: Also add a lint rule in our infra admission controller to warn when a VPA in Auto exists for a deployment with HPA present.
anya: Good call. Also add a runbook entry: if CA launches >10 GPU nodes in 10m, check HPA metrics, VPA recommendations, and recent rollouts.
mike: thanks all, cost blip contained. :thumbsup:
